claim: An attacker who obtains a never-expiring API key calls the inference gateway as that team indefinitely.
notes: Bearer credential with no expiry on an internet-facing endpoint; compromise is permanent until noticed.

claim: Any workload inside the model network submits inference requests posing as the gateway, which the model server accepts on network position alone.
notes: Stated absence of authentication behind a boundary that is only 'meant to be' closed.

claim: An attacker publishes a model artifact under a shared group account with no individual identity behind it.
notes: Publish authentication is unknown and possibly shared; report as unverified.

claim: An attacker who can write to the registry swaps the model artifact and the model server loads it without any integrity verification.
notes: The defining supply-chain finding of this case; the source states verification is absent.

claim: An attacker with model-network access writes to the unauthenticated Redis feature store and changes the features a decision is made on.
notes: No password is a stated fact, not an unknown; poisoning features silently changes inference output.

claim: An attacker inside the model network alters request payloads in flight on the unauthenticated, unencrypted forward path.
notes: Same flow as the spoofing entry; the lane difference is modifying content versus assuming identity.

claim: Nobody can establish which engineer published a given model artifact, because publication runs through a shared account.
notes: Model provenance is the audit trail that matters here; a shared account destroys it.

claim: A calling team disputes a request the log attributes to them, and a shared long-lived API key cannot establish who actually sent it.
notes: The log records the key's team, not an actor; distinct from disclosure findings about the same store.

claim: An attacker who reaches the inference log reads raw end-user prompts, whose protection at rest is unverified.
notes: A debugging store that silently became the most sensitive data collection in the system.

claim: An attacker with model-network access reads per-customer account age and spend bands from the unauthenticated feature store.
notes: Stated absence of authentication over data tagged pii and financial.

claim: A caller crafts a request that makes the model emit customer features belonging to a different tenant.
notes: Model-mediated disclosure: the gateway authenticates the team but nothing scopes which customers' features a request may pull. Review sitting 01 struck 'or training data' from this claim: no training pipeline exists in this model, and the label set already rules training-time attacks out of scope for this case, so the claim graded the tool against a fact the model does not hold.

claim: An attacker on the internal path reads end-user text out of forwarded requests, because transport encryption there is unverified.
notes: Boundary crossing from serving edge into model network with no stated protection.

claim: A caller holding a valid key floods the gateway with inference requests and exhausts the shared GPU capacity behind it.
notes: GPU capacity is the scarce, expensive resource; no quota or rate limit per key is described.

claim: An attacker with model-network access flushes or fills the unauthenticated Redis store, stalling every request that needs features.
notes: An unauthenticated cache is as easy to destroy as to read.

claim: An attacker deletes or corrupts the registry artifact so the model server cannot start after a restart.
notes: Startup dependency with no fallback described.

claim: An attacker who can write to the registry turns an unverified artifact load into code execution on the GPU nodes.
notes: Model artifacts are loaded as code; the escalation framing of the swap finding.

claim: An attacker who compromises the internet-facing gateway inherits unauthenticated access to everything in the model network.
notes: The whole model network's security rests on the gateway being the only reachable path.

claim: A caller uses its key to reach models or capabilities its team was never entitled to, because the key authenticates without scoping what it may invoke.
notes: Authorization scope on a multi-tenant gateway is unspecified; report as unverified.
